1. Unscrew the top cap (counter-clockwise, four full turns) and lift the globe (part G-600)
straight up.
2. The globe gasket is part G-600G. Lift it out with the pick, not with a screwdriver.
Replace it if it is flattened, cracked, or if there was water in the base.
3. Seat the new G-600G in the channel with the lip facing up. Press it down all the way
round.
4. Fit the globe and screw the cap down until it stops, then back it off a quarter turn so
the gasket is not crushed.
5. Water test: run the shower head over the lantern for 2 minutes on the wet bench, then
open it and check the base is dry. The Beacon 600 is rated IPX5 and a repaired one
must meet it.
Battery contacts
1. Remove the base plate (three Phillips screws, 0.6 N·m on refit).
2. If a cell has leaked, neutralise the deposit with the vinegar swab, then rinse with the
contact cleaner and dry.
3. Brush the four contacts and the two springs with the fibre brush until they are bright.
4. Fit four fresh test cells from the bench stock, check the lantern lights on both levels
and in red night mode, then remove the test cells. We do not ship the Beacon 600 with
cells.
Sentinel 1000 and 1000 Pro

Sentinel 1000 and 1000 Pro
The Sentinel 1000 (LS-1000) and Sentinel 1000 Pro (LS-1000P) share one body and one
service procedure; the Pro has the larger pack, four light panels instead of two, and the solar
top. They carry a 5-year warranty, so most Sentinels on the bench are red tags. The faults are
a pack that will not hold charge, a panel latch that will not hold a panel, and the charge port.
Tools: a T8 Torx driver, the plastic spudger, the pack tester, and the latch spring tool.
Battery pack
The Sentinel 1000 battery pack is part B-1000-21 and is held by four T8 Torx screws. The
Pro's pack is part B-1000P-21, same mounting. A pack tests bad if it holds less than 70% of
its rated capacity after a full charge on the pack tester, or if it is swollen at all.
1. Discharge the lantern to below 20% on low before opening it. The charge indicator
shows one bar.

2. Open the base: the four T8 Torx screws are under the rubber feet. Lift the feet with the
spudger and keep them; they are not sold separately.
3. Lift the pack out by the pull tab and unplug the three-pin connector. Do not pull on the
wires.
4. Fit the new B-1000-21 (or B-1000P-21), connect, and run the self-test by holding the
power button for 8 seconds. Four blinks is a pass.
5. Refit the screws to 0.5 N·m and press the feet back on.
6. A bad pack goes to the LI cabinet with the ticket number written on it in marker.
Panel latch
1. Each detachable panel is held by a latch with a spring (part L-1000S). A panel that
drops when the lantern is tilted has a tired spring.
2. Remove the panel. Press the latch tab in with the spring tool and lift the latch out.
3. Fit the new spring with the long leg toward the body, press the latch back until it clicks.
4. Fit the panel, invert the lantern and shake it gently. The panel must stay put.
Charge port
The USB-C charge port is on a small board (part PCB-1000C) and is replaced as a unit. A

The Beacon 600 is our camp lantern: big enough to light a four-person tent or a picnic shelter,
heavy enough to stay put in wind. Four D cells last five nights of evening use on high, and on low
the lantern runs for five days straight. The red night mode keeps night vision while you find your
way to the car. A steel hanging hook screws into the top, and the shoulder strap clips to the bail.
The globe is glass, which gives a cleaner light than polycarbonate but can break; a replacement
globe is part G-600 and fits in two minutes with no tools. Batteries are not included because D
cells ship badly and most customers have a preference.

Compatible parts: globe G-600, hanging hook H-600, shoulder strap S-600.

The Sentinel 1000 is the lantern we sell to people who lose power often. Its two light panels pull
off the body and run on their own for up to 6 hours each, so one lantern lights the kitchen while a
panel goes to the bathroom and another to the stairs. The body is sealed to IP67 and floats. The
10,000 mAh battery charges over USB-C in about 7 hours and can run a phone from the USB-A port for
several days. The Sentinel line carries a 5-year warranty on the lantern and panels; the battery,
as on every rechargeable product, is covered for 1 year.

Compatible parts: USB-C cable C-15, replacement panel P-1000, carry bag BG-1000.

The Sentinel 1000 Pro doubles the battery and the panel count of the Sentinel 1000 and adds a
4-watt solar panel in the lid. In full sun the solar top adds about 2 hours of high-mode runtime
per day, which is not enough to run the lantern on sun alone but will keep it topped up between
outages. Four panels mean four rooms lit from one base. At 1.9 kg it is a lantern to carry to the
car, not up a trail. Same IP67 sealing and the same 5-year warranty as the Sentinel 1000.

Compatible parts: USB-C cable C-15, replacement panel P-1000, carry bag BG-1000P.

### Scenario 1: a return just outside the window

On Monday, October 12, 2026, a customer emails about order LS-2026-008316, a Beacon 600 ordered
on August 20 and delivered on August 29. She wants to return it because she bought a Sentinel 1000
instead. Forty days from August 29 is October 8, so the window closed four days before she wrote.
The agent replies with RET-01, adjusted: the lantern is unused and boxed, so the agent offers,
with the shift lead's okay, an exchange toward the Sentinel 1000 as a one-time courtesy, with the
12% restocking fee waived because it is an exchange. The customer accepts. The agent issues
RA-121877, offers the $8.50 prepaid label, and notes the courtesy on the ticket. The exchange
difference is charged when the Beacon 600 arrives at Hagerstown.

### Scenario 2: a Sentinel 1000 Pro that stopped charging

On Thursday, September 3, 2026, a customer calls about a Sentinel 1000 Pro bought on June 14,
2025, order LS-2025-002210. It no longer charges from the wall or the solar top. The lantern is
inside its 5-year warranty, but the battery pack is inside its own 1-year battery warranty only
until June 14, 2026, which has passed. The agent opens warranty claim WC-030517 anyway, because
the fault may be the charging circuit rather than the pack, and explains that the Repair Center
will decide within 5 business days. On September 8 Walt Brannigan's team finds a failed charge
controller, which is a manufacturing defect covered by the 5-year warranty, and repairs it at no
charge under repair ticket RT-20931. The lantern ships back on September 11. Had the fault been
the pack alone, the agent would have quoted a paid pack replacement instead.

### Lost in transit

A package counts as lost when it has not arrived 10 business days after the expected delivery
date shown in tracking. Before that, ask the customer to check with neighbors and the carrier.
Once a package is lost, ship a replacement first and file the carrier claim afterwards; the
customer does not wait for the carrier. Note the carrier claim number on the ticket. If the
replacement is also fuel, confirm the address is not a PO box.

A package shown as delivered that the customer says did not arrive is handled the same way after
a 2-business-day wait, with one exception: for orders over $400, which require a signature, pull
the signature image from the carrier before replacing.

## Warranty claims

The standard warranty is 2 years from the purchase date and covers manufacturing defects. The
Sentinel 1000 and Sentinel 1000 Pro carry 5 years, the Heritage No. 7 carries 10 years,
rechargeable batteries and battery packs carry 1 year, and Second Light refurbished items carry
1 year. Mantles, globes, wicks, bulbs and fuel caps are consumables and are not covered. Drops,
water beyond the IP rating, unapproved fuel, modifications and commercial rental use are not
covered.

A customer starts a claim by emailing help@lanternsupply.example with the order number and
photos. Open a warranty claim in the Hearth admin; it issues a number in the form WC-xxxxxx, for
example WC-030517. The Repair Center decides within 5 business days whether to repair or replace,
and the choice is ours. For an approved claim, send the customer a prepaid label to the
Hagerstown Repair Center at no charge. A claim with no order number can be matched by email
address or by the serial number on the base of the lantern.

The warranty transfers with a gift but not with a resale. If a customer bought the item second
hand, explain this and offer a paid repair.

## Repairs

Any repair, under warranty or paid, gets a repair ticket in the form RT-xxxxx (five digits), for
example RT-20931. Create it in the Hearth admin from the warranty claim or from scratch for a paid
repair. The ticket number goes on the box and in the email to the customer.

Customers can drop a lantern off at either showroom or mail it to Lantern Supply Co. Repair
Center, 1180 Downsville Pike, Dock B, Hagerstown, MD 21740. Annapolis drop-offs are shipped to
Hagerstown weekly on Tuesdays, so tell Annapolis customers to add a week. Walt Brannigan, Head
of Repairs, emails a quote for paid repairs before any work is done; nothing is charged until the
customer approves the quote. Fuel lanterns must be emptied before they are mailed; tell the
customer, and put it in the email.
